title: Turn a synthetic focus group into a real test plan
goal: Use varied constraints to brainstorm hypotheses while avoiding fake participants and reactions.
explanation: A model cannot reveal what real people subconsciously think. Simulated personas are a brainstorming aid shaped by the prompt, not representative research or testimonials. Vary relevant needs such as time, readability and trust instead of relying on demographic stereotypes. Design a real consented test to evaluate the hypotheses.
sampleInput: Fictional slogan: “One small build. One useful skill.” Test contexts: a rushed first-time learner; a reader using a small phone with low bandwidth; a cautious learner concerned about credentials and privacy. No person has actually reviewed the slogan.
prompt: Generate possible reactions for these three fictional contexts. Label every reaction Hypothesis, not a quote from a participant. For each, list a neutral question and an observable test. Do not infer subconscious feelings, population preferences or purchase intent. Do not invent survey counts or ratings.
workedExample: Hypothesis: “useful skill” may feel too vague. Neutral question: “What would you expect to do after reading this?” Observable test: ask consented readers to describe the expected activity before showing the course list. Three simulated reactions are not three participants.

steps.title: Define relevant contexts
steps.text: Use task constraints rather than stereotypes about age, gender or occupation.

steps.title: Generate labelled hypotheses
steps.text: Keep the fictional nature visible on every reaction.

steps.title: Write neutral questions
steps.text: Avoid asking whether the reader likes your preferred wording.

steps.title: Plan an observable task
steps.text: Choose what a real reader will do or explain and decide how to record consent and feedback.

steps.title: Report honestly
steps.text: Keep simulation notes separate from any later human evidence, including sample limits and negative feedback.

checks: All synthetic reactions are labelled hypotheses with no invented participant quotes or counts.
Each context produces a neutral question and an observable test.
The final plan separates brainstorming from actual consented user research.
commonMistakes: Reporting a synthetic focus group as representative market evidence.
Attributing hidden psychological reactions to demographic stereotypes.
offline: Brainstorm the three context-based hypotheses yourself and write the same real-user test plan.
reflection: What result from real readers would make you abandon the slogan?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. All synthetic reactions are labelled hypotheses with no invented participant quotes or counts.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Each context produces a neutral question and an observable test.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Reporting a synthetic focus group as representative market evidence.

editorialStatus: Original authored activity; independent subject-matter review and learner timing remain pending.
providerNote: Materials are free. External tools may require an adult account, credits, regional eligibility or a paid plan. Check current terms before using them. Do not paste passwords, API keys, private messages or other people’s personal data. No model runs locally or downloads automatically on this platform.
completionNote: Completion is a learner self-report based on saved evidence, not verified assessment or an accredited credential.
